findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0326: References to APIs Allowing Fallback to Non-Biometric Authentication
findings.explanation:
The shared BiometricDeviceAuthentication allows DEVICE_CREDENTIAL alongside biometrics. It gates screen lock, payment lock, payment confirmation, payments recovery phrase and device linking, so a device PIN is enough for those operations. MASTG treats this as a hardening weakness.
app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/BiometricDeviceAuthentication.kt:29: Allowed authenticators include DEVICE_CREDENTIAL.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0327: References to APIs for Event-Bound Biometric Authentication
findings.explanation:
BiometricPrompt.authenticate is called without a CryptoObject, and no Keystore key uses setUserAuthenticationRequired(true). Success depends only on the callback, for screen lock, payment confirmation and device linking.
app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/BiometricDeviceAuthentication.kt:83: Event-bound biometric prompt without a CryptoObject.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0329: References to APIs Enforcing Authentication without Explicit User Action
findings.explanation:
setConfirmationRequired(false) is set on the prompt that authorizes MobileCoin payments and the one that reveals the payments recovery phrase. Passive biometrics such as face unlock can then approve these without an explicit confirm tap.
app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/payments/confirm/ConfirmPaymentFragment.java:147: Payment confirmation prompt doesn't require explicit confirmation.
app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/payments/backup/PaymentsRecoveryStartFragment.java:73: Recovery-phrase prompt doesn't require explicit confirmation.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0208: Insufficient Key Sizes
findings.explanation:
The legacy local encryption key (MasterSecret) is generated as AES-128. The Keystore wrapping key in KeyStoreHelper doesn't set a key size, so it also defaults to 128-bit AES. MASTG counts 128-bit AES as insufficient against quantum attacks.
app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/crypto/MasterSecretUtil.java:251: MasterSecret encryption key generated with a 128-bit AES key size.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0235: Android App Configurations Allowing Cleartext Traffic
findings.explanation:
android:usesCleartextTraffic is true and no network security config limits it.
app/src/nightlyStaging/AndroidManifest.xml:6: android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0285: Outdated Android Version Allowing Trust in User-Provided CAs
findings.explanation:
minSdk is 23 (< 24), so on Android 6 the default config trusts user-installed CAs. Signal's own service connections use dedicated TrustStores, which limits the impact; WebViews and third-party endpoints use the platform default. Ward's analyzer said: Whether user-installed CAs are trusted by default depends on targetSdk (trusted below 24), which Ward couldn't resolve.
gradle/libs.versions.toml:9: minSdk below 24.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0381: References to Insecure PendingIntent Creation
findings.explanation:
minSdk is 23, and the shared PendingIntentFlags.mutable() helper returns FLAG_MUTABLE on API 31+ and 0 (mutable) below. It is used for dozens of notification content intents and alarms that don't need mutability. Base intents are mostly explicit, which reduces but doesn't remove the risk.
core/util/src/main/java/org/signal/core/util/PendingIntentFlags.kt:40: Default helper makes PendingIntents mutable on every API level.
app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/gcm/FcmFetchManager.kt:100: Notification content intent created mutable without need.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0202: References to APIs and Permissions for Accessing External Storage
findings.explanation:
The app declares WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdk 28, minSdk 23) and QuickstartCredentialExporter writes the account's identity private keys, service password, profile key and account entropy pool as plaintext JSON to getExternalFilesDir(), which other apps with storage permission can read on API 23-28. It is reached from the internal settings screen but compiled into the release source set. SaveAttachmentUtil's public-directory writes are user-initiated media exports.
app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/registration/data/QuickstartCredentialExporter.kt:65: Credential export targets app-specific external storage.
app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/registration/data/QuickstartCredentialExporter.kt:67: Private keys, service password and AEP are written unencrypted.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:71: External storage write permission declared for API <= 28.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0216: Sensitive Data Not Excluded From Backup
findings.explanation:
The release manifest enables backup with a key-value BackupAgent whose only item is SvrAuthTokens, so SVR2 authentication credentials are uploaded to and restored from Android Backup. This looks like an intentional choice so a PIN-based re-registration can skip SMS. The team should still confirm it accepts credentials in cloud backup. Ward's analyzer said: Backup is on with backup rules. Check that the rules exclude credentials, tokens and other sensitive files.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:78: Custom key-value backup agent registered.
app/src/main/java/org/thoughtcrime/securesms/absbackup/backupables/SvrAuthTokens.kt:20: SVR2 auth tokens are serialized into the backup payload.
demo/camera/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:19: rules file @xml/data_extraction_rules
demo/camera/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:20: rules file @xml/backup_rules

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0262: References to Backup Configurations Not Excluding Sensitive Data
findings.explanation:
android:allowBackup is true in the release manifest and SignalBackupAgent backs up SvrAuthTokens (SVR2 credentials) to Android Backup. These are credentials, not excluded data. The demo/camera rules files the analyzer cited belong to a demo module that isn't shipped. Ward's analyzer said: Backup is on with backup rules. Check that the rules exclude credentials, tokens and other sensitive files.
